nodes.name: NiFe-O nanosheet growth
nodes.procedure: The nickel chloride solution with pH of 6.2 was prepared by dissolving 10 mmol NiCl₂·6H₂O in 10 mL deionized water in a 50 mL beaker. Next, the Fe foam with a tailored area of 2×3 cm² was soaked in this solution at room temperature for 5 min (optimized), during which NiFe-O nanoarrays were in situ grown on the Fe foam.
nodes.source_text: Fe foam... was soaked in this solution at room temperature for 5, 30, 60 min... optimized parameters (1 M NiCl₂, 5 min soaking)

nodes.name: Fe-O nanosheet growth
nodes.procedure: The control sample of Fe-O NAs/Fe foam was prepared by soaking Fe foam in NaCl solution (pH = 7) with the same chloride concentration of NiCl2 solution for 5 min.
nodes.source_text: To explore the role of Ni²⁺ and Cl⁻ in sample preparation... Fe-O NAs/Fe foam was prepared by soaking Fe foam in NaCl solution (pH = 7)...

nodes.name: Post-synthesis washing and drying
nodes.procedure: NiFe-O NAs/Fe foam and Fe-O NAs/Fe foam were obtained after washing repeatedly with water and drying in air at 60°C for 1 h.

unit_operations.name: Drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: drying in air at 60°C for 1 h

nodes.source_text: Finally, NiFe-O NAs/Fe foam and Fe-O NAs/Fe foam were obtained after washing repeatedly with water and drying in air at 60°C for 1 h.

nodes.name: NiFe-P phosphorization
nodes.procedure: NiFe-P NAs/Fe foam was obtained by low-temperature phosphorization of NiFe-O NAs/Fe foam in a chemical vapor deposition system. Typically, the sample was placed at the downstream side, while NaH₂PO₂ (0.9 g) was placed at the upstream side of the furnace tube. Subsequently, the sample was heated to 300°C for 0.5 h at a heating rate of 2°C min⁻¹ in 30 sccm Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: NiFe-P NAs/Fe foam was obtained by low-temperature phosphorization... heated to 300°C for 0.5 h... 30 sccm Ar atmosphere.

nodes.source_text: Fe-P NAs/Fe foam and P-Fe foam with no nanoarray structure were respectively prepared by phosphating Fe-O NAs/Fe foam and bare Fe foam under similar condition.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform and high-density NiFe-O NAs vertically grown on Fe foam with length of hundreds of nanometers and diameter of 20-30 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b shows that uniform and high-density NiFe-O NAs are vertically grown on Fe foam with the length of hundreds of nanometers and diameter of 20 - 30 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM observation and SAED identification reveal amorphous feature of NiFe-O NAs with no lattice fringe and diffuse halo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM observation and SAED identification reveal the amorphous feature of NiFe-O NAs with no lattice fringe and diffuse halo (Fig. 1c, d).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-P NAs preserve nanowire morphology after phosphorization with larger diameter of 50-100 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After phosphorization, NiFe-P NAs preserve nanowire morphology and amorphous feature with the larger diameter of 50 - 100 nm (Fig. 1e-g).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and SAED confirm amorphous feature of NiFe-P NAs after phosphorization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After phosphorization, NiFe-P NAs preserve nanowire morphology and amorphous feature with the larger diameter of 50 - 100 nm (Fig. 1e-g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distributions of Ni, Fe, P (and/or O) elements in NiFe-X NAs with ultralow atomic content of Ni (0.28-0.36%) and Ni:Fe < 0.015:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX characterizations of NiFe-X (X = O, P) NAs show the uniform distributions of Ni, Fe, P (and/or O) elements (Fig. 1h and Fig. S5, S6). The ultralow atomic content of Ni (0.28 - 0.36%) and ultralow nickel iron ratio (Ni:Fe < 0.015:1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Only Fe peaks from substrate visible; no other distinct peaks confirming amorphous nature of NiFe-X (X = O,P) NAs consistent with SAED.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides the two peaks of Fe (PDF#01-1267) originated from Fe foam in the XRD patterns of Fe foam, NiFe-O NAs/Fe foam and NiFe-P NAs/Fe foam (Fig. S9), there are no other distinct peaks. This suggests the amorphous feature of NiFe-X (X = O,P) NAs which is well consistent with the SAED results in Fig. 1d, g.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-O NAs mainly contain Fe2O3 and α-FeOOH (corrosion products of Fe in NiCl2 solution).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of NiFe-O NAs/Fe foam suggest that NiFe-O NAs mainly contain Fe2O3 and α-FeOOH (the corrosion products of Fe in NiCl2 solution), which are consistent with the observed XPS peaks assigned to Fe2+, Fe3+, Fe-Ox, and Fe-OH units (Fig. 2a and Fig. S10a,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe2+, Fe3+, Fe-Ox, Fe-OH units detected; weak Ni2+ signal indicates doping state and ultra-low Ni content; Fe 2p peaks shift ~0.55 eV higher confirming strong Ni-Fe electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, no obvious characteristics associated to the Ni compounds are observed in Raman spectra while weak XPS signal for Ni2+ is clearly detected (Fig. S10b); this indicates the doping state and ultra-low content of Ni in NiFe-O NAs. Further, the Fe 2p peaks in NiFe-O NAs/Fe foam shift to higher binding energies (~ 0.55 eV) with respect to the Fe-O NAs/Fe foam counterpart.

nodes.characterization_summary: Only P-O and Fe-O peaks detected; no observable peaks for iron phosphide or nickel phosphide due to their metal-like feature and high electrical conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For NiFe-P NAs, only Raman peaks originated from P-O and Fe-O are found while no observable Raman peaks for iron phosphide or nickel phosphide are detected due to their metal-like feature and high electrical conductivity (Fig. 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-P NAs mainly consist of FeP, Fe-Ox, Fe-Pox and trace Ni compounds; Fe-P binding energy close to metallic Fe0 suggesting partially charged Fe species; Ni2+ and Ni3+ (not Ni0) detected indicating trace Ni doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, the XPS results (Fig. 2d and Fig. S10d-f) reveal NiFe-P NAs mainly consist of FeP, Fe - Ox, and Fe - POx and trace amounts of similar Ni compounds. In addition, the binding energy of Fe-P in NiFe-P NAs is close to that of metallic Fe0, suggesting the existence of partially charged Fe species. Besides, Ni2+ and Ni3+ species rather than metallic Ni0 were detected in the Ni 2p spectrum of NiFe-P NAs, indicating the doping state of trace Ni in NiFe-P NAs.
